verbose.description: Legacy switch: true selects trace, false selects info. An explicit logging.level takes priority. Also controlled with --verbose / --no-verbose.

level.description: Minimum server-console/Warden severity. Null uses the legacy verbose switch. --log-level or OP77_CONFIG__LOGGING__LEVEL also sets this field.

icon.description: Relative PNG path, square, at most 256 KiB. Warden enforces exactly the bounds below on upload (Branding/BrandingConstraints.cs); the loader below is looser, which is the trap. USE 64-512 px per side: this server accepts 32-512 (ServerIconLoader) but the website's display guard rejects anything under 64 on the shorter side (app/src/lib/server-images.ts), so only the overlap actually renders and a 32-48 px icon validates here then silently shows a placeholder on the site. That guard also rejects a longer/shorter skew above 1.2, so keep it exactly square. 256x256 recommended.

banner.description: Relative PNG/JPEG/WebP path for the wide hero image; width 320-4096 px, aspect 2.0-5.0 and at most 2 MiB. 1200x400 (3:1) is the recommended size. BUDGET, and it binds far tighter than the 2 MiB: the icon and the banner travel base64-encoded inside ONE registration request, and the master caps a request body at 512 KiB (master/src/Open77.Master/Program.cs), so the two files together must stay under ~378 KiB of raw bytes. Over that, the registration is refused with a bare HTTP 413 and the server does not appear in the catalogue AT ALL -- a worse failure than having no branding. Warden checks the pair before writing; a hand-placed pair is flagged at startup. See Branding/BrandingConstraints.cs.

publicEndpoint.description: Public hostname or IP with port, e.g. play.example.net:11778.

maximumAiVehiclesPerSimulator.description: Admission slots per native AI simulator, including pending traffic placements. Healthy existing owners are retained. The default is the server's own per-simulator ceiling of 128; the server has no total driver-job limit.

playerInterestDeferredBootstrap.description: With a positive player interest radius, wait for placement before announcing nearby peers instead of seeding the full bucket on admission.

combat.description: Server-wide combat policy for car impacts on players. Optional; every field defaults to the behaviour before it existed.

vehicleHitCreditsDriver.description: Credit the seated driver the server finds behind a car impact as the attacker, through the ordinary PvP policy (friendly fire, teams, combat scopes, god mode, resource arbiters, per-victim caps); death cause becomes vehicle. False keeps the impact the victim's own environment hit. The culprit is published to resources either way (open77:playerHitByVehicle).

vehicleHitSpeedDamage.description: Price an identified car impact from the server-observed relative speed with the curve below. False keeps the flat 10 HP vanilla 2.31 applies.

vehicleHitDamageFloor.description: Health points at and below vehicleHitDamageFloorSpeed.

vehicleHitDamageFloorSpeed.description: Metres per second up to which the floor price applies.

vehicleHitDamageCap.description: Health points at and above vehicleHitDamageCapSpeed (linear in between). Keep it below the maximum health pool if one impact from full health must never kill.

vehicleHitDamageCapSpeed.description: Metres per second from which the cap applies; must exceed vehicleHitDamageFloorSpeed.

vehicleHitAudit.description: Log-only count of suspected car strikes nobody reported (a driven vehicle's server path crossing a living player at speed with no impact report). Changes no damage.

handheldDischarges.description: Admit handheld discharge declarations: the server binds each living body, sends its client the binding, and admits fire declarations against the drawn catalogued weapon and a per-class cadence. A receipt damages nothing by itself; platform-priced NPC hits require one, and handheldVehicleDamage consumes them. False: no binding is sent and platform-priced NPCs cannot be priced from a player's hit.

handheldVehicleDamage.description: Apply a handheld gun hit on a car another client simulates (or nobody does) to the canonical vehicle health, consuming one admitted discharge receipt per car. Requires handheldDischarges. Off until two-client live acceptance.

replication.description: Protocol38 replication rollback switches. Optional; every field defaults to the shipped behaviour. Each switch takes one protocol38 mechanism back to what it replaced, without a rebuild. A field left out or null keeps the legacy environment variable where one exists (OP77_CONTACT_STEWARD, OP77_CONTACT_EPISODES, OP77_GNS_TRAFFIC_LANES: exactly 0 turns the switch off), then the default; an explicit value always wins over the environment. Read once at startup: restart to apply.

contactSteward.description: Contact steward: an unattended car about to be struck is simulated by the approaching driver, so observers see it pushed. False: the struck car stays at owner 0 and moves on the striker's screen only. Legacy fallback: OP77_CONTACT_STEWARD=0.

contactEpisodes.description: Cross-reporter contact episode arbitration: both owners' reports of one car/car crash become one event. False: every accepted report is its own event and the counterpart is delivered at once. Legacy fallback: OP77_CONTACT_EPISODES=0.

trafficLanes.description: GNS traffic lanes (ordered, timed motion, voice) on connections opened afterwards. False: every new connection keeps the native single lane. Legacy fallback: OP77_GNS_TRAFFIC_LANES=0.

hitRewindStrict.description: Strict hit rewind: a player hit must match the victim's rewound path; the newest pose is no longer an alternative. False keeps the rewind never stricter than the check it replaced.

timedMotionWindowMs.description: Native send-queue allowance of a timed motion batch, in milliseconds. 15 is the rollback of the near-lane phase. Above the 40 ms reliable window, motion can delay reliable traffic by the difference.

timedVehicleValidationTicks.description: Vehicle scopes are revalidated every this many server ticks, viewers sliced (5 Hz at the default 30 Hz tick). 1 restores per-tick validation.

timedStarvationShareMs.description: After this many milliseconds without a timed motion admission while reliable traffic holds the link, one timed batch may pass. 0 restores the strict reliable-always-first rule; otherwise 10 to 1000.

load.description: Ordered resource directory rules. Entries add matches; a leading ! removes them. Paths are relative to resources.root unless absolute and support *, ? and **.

requiredMods.description: The mods every player must load to join this world. Absent or empty means 'requires nothing', which is what every server means until an owner opts in.

unsecured.description: UNSECURED MODE. Lets this server require executable packages that carry no verified attestation (and lets a resource preload them). Every server list shows the server with an 'unsecured' flag and players must confirm the risk before joining. Off by default.

items.description: Two custody models. An 'indexed' package names an entry in the platform's signed index and may carry only minVersion; a 'hosted' package is served by this server and must pin version, sha256 and sizeBytes.

file.description: Relative JSONC file containing authenticated public-key ACL principals.

connectionString.description: MySQL connection string used by resources with the database.access permission.

http.description: Outbound HTTP for resources holding the http.request permission (PerformHttpRequest). Off by default; nothing is reachable until allowedHosts names a destination. Redirects are never followed.

allowedHosts.description: Exact hosts (discord.com) or one level of subdomain (*.example.com). No scheme, path or port.

httpHandlers.description: Inbound HTTP for resources holding the http.serve permission (Open77.http.listen / SetHttpHandler). Off by default and bound to loopback by default; plain HTTP with no authentication, so anything reachable from the internet goes behind a reverse proxy. Routes are /<resource>/<prefix>.

listenUrl.description: Absolute http:// origin the listener binds, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11781. No https, no path.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long a request waits for its Lua handler before the server answers 504 handler_timeout on its behalf.

metrics.description: Independent read-only Prometheus endpoint at /metrics. Disabled by default; no Warden session or running capture required.

listenUrl.description: One HTTP origin with an IP literal or localhost. Remote binding requires a bearer token; terminate TLS at a reverse proxy.

tokenEnvironmentVariable.description: Environment variable containing a 32–256 character bearer token. Missing is permitted only on loopback. Never put the token itself in this file.

warden.description: The Warden in-process admin panel. Off by default.

hubFileGatewayOrigin.description: Trusted Hub file gateway origin. HTTPS, or HTTP with an explicit loopback IP for local testing. No path, credentials, query or fragment. Omit to disable Hub installation.

listenUrl.description: Absolute HTTP URL the admin panel binds, e.g. http://0.0.0.0:11780.

rcon.description: Authenticated Open77 TCP RCON for dashboard backends, independent of the Warden HTTP listener. Secrets are read from environment variables.

bindAddress.description: IPv4 or IPv6 literal. Non-loopback plaintext requires allowInsecureRemote.

tlsCertificateFile.description: PFX/PKCS#12 certificate with private key; relative to the configuration directory.

convars.description: FiveM-style convars: a flat name/value bag of strings read from Lua by GetConvar, GetConvarInt and GetConvarBool. This is a COMPATIBILITY SHIM so a resource ported from FiveM runs without its configuration layer being rewritten; it is not the mechanism to reach for when writing something new. Open77.tunables is better on every axis that matters -- a tunable is declared with a type and a range, validated on every write, retunable by the operator from the Warden panel while the server runs, persisted across a restart, and scoped to the resource that declared it, which also receives onTunableChanged. A convar is an untyped string, server-wide, and a SetConvar from Lua is in-memory only and gone on the next restart. Keep it credential-free -- this file is tracked, so a token or password belongs in the environment like every other credential in this schema.

startup.description: What this server does to itself once it has finished starting.

commands.description: Console commands run once, in order, after resources have started -- the server-side equivalent of exec in a server.cfg. Each line goes through the same dispatcher as a line typed at the stdin console and carries exactly that authority, never a player's. Per server by design: this is how a gamemode's host pins world state (for example Pursuit's fixed clock and weather) without editing a resource every other server also loads. A line the dispatcher refuses is logged as an error and the server starts anyway. Keep it credential-free -- this file is tracked, so a token or password belongs in the environment.

serverId.description: Stable server identity issued or approved by the Master.

identityFile.description: Relative file used for the automatically generated Master identity.

licenseKey.description: Platform license key created in the keymaster. Prefer the environment variable so this file stays credential-free.

licenseKeyEnvironmentVariable.description: Environment variable consulted when licenseKey is not set (default OP77_LICENSE_KEY).

requireConnectTicket.description: Require a valid master-signed connect ticket in ClientHello to join.

publishPlayerList.description: Publish the display names of the players currently online with the heartbeat, so the server's public page shows who is on and not just how many. Default true: those names are already visible to everyone in the world and joining is free. Nothing else is published - no account id, no address, no position. Set false and the directory answers players: null, which is distinct from an empty roster.

devLocalAuth.description: Local development bypass. When true the server accepts unauthenticated clients (no master certificate, no connect ticket) and binds the game socket to loopback only. Accepted ONLY when enabled=false, visibility=private and requireConnectTicket=false; never usable on a public/mastered server. For agent/MCP local dev without the prod launcher.
